intended_object: For i0 ≤ j in a directed preorder, this is the inclusion functor from the tail {k | j ≤ k} into the tail {k | i0 ≤ k}, both viewed as preorder categories. The docstring and the module docs present it as a tool for changing the base index of a colimit over tails.
explanation: The body is right: it sends k to ⟨k.1, h.trans k.2⟩, which is monotone, and `Monotone.functor` turns that into the inclusion functor between the two preorder categories. Its only role is technical. The library proves the functor is final (`betweenTailInclusion_final`) so it can move colimits of the "cylinder sections" diagram from the tail at i0 to the tail at j. That makes it an auxiliary device for one proof, not a mathematical notion in its own right. It is just the inclusion of one sub-preorder into another, and Mathlib could produce it directly from `Set.inclusion` together with `Monotone.functor`. The construction has nothing to object to, and there is no standalone notion here to compare it against.
